```text
func (ctx *preReceiveContext) canWriteCodeUnit() bool {
	if ctx.canWriteCodeUnitCached == nil {
		canWrite := ctx.userPerm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) || ctx.deployKeyAccessMode >= perm_model.AccessModeWrite
		ctx.canWriteCodeUnitCached = &canWrite
	}
	return *ctx.canWriteCodeUnitCached
}

// canWriteCodeRef returns true if pusher can write to the code ref (branch/tag/commit)
func (ctx *preReceiveContext) canWriteCodeRef(refFullName git.RefName) bool {
	if ctx.canWriteCodeUnit() {
		return true
	}
	// then check whether if the pusher is a maintainer who can write the PR author's head repo branch
	if !refFullName.IsBranch() {
		return false
	}
	return issues_model.CanMaintainerWriteToBranch(ctx, ctx.userPerm, refFullName.BranchName(), ctx.user)
}

// assertCanWriteRef returns true if pusher can write to the code ref, otherwise it responds with 403 Forbidden and returns false
func (ctx *preReceiveContext) assertCanWriteRef(refFullName git.RefName) bool {
	if !ctx.canWriteCodeRef(refFullName) {
		if ctx.Written() {
			return false
		}
		ctx.JSON(http.StatusForbidden, private.Response{
			UserMsg: "User permission denied for writing.",
		})
		return false
	}
	return true
}

// CanCreatePullRequest returns true if pusher can create pull requests

	if !ctx.checkedCanCreatePullRequest {

		ctx.checkedCanCreatePullRequest = true
	}
	return ctx.canCreatePullRequest
```

```text
	if err != nil {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid token")
	}

	claims, claimsOk := token.Claims.(*Claims)
	if !token.Valid || !claimsOk {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid token claim")
	}

	if claims.RepoID != target.ID {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid token claim")
	}

	if mode == perm_model.AccessModeWrite && claims.Op != "upload" {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid token claim")
	}

	u, err := user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, claims.UserID)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error("Unable to GetUserById[%d]: Error: %v", claims.UserID, err)
		return nil, err
	}
	if !u.IsActive || u.ProhibitLogin {
		return nil, util.NewPermissionDeniedErrorf("not allowed to access any repository")
	}

	perm, err := access_model.GetDoerRepoPermission(ctx, target, u)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error("Unable to GetDoerRepoPermission for user[%d] repo[%d]: %v", claims.UserID, target.ID, err)
		return nil, err
	}
	if !perm.CanAccess(mode, unit.TypeCode) {
		return nil, util.NewPermissionDeniedErrorf("no permission to access the repository")
	}
	return u, nil
}

func parseToken(ctx stdCtx.Context, authorization string, target *repo_model.Repository, mode perm_model.AccessMode) (*user_model.User, error) {
	if authorization == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("no token")
	}
	parsed, ok := httpauth.ParseAuthorizationHeader(authorization)
	if !ok || parsed.BearerToken == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("token not found")
	}
	return handleLFSToken(ctx, parsed.BearerToken.Token, target, mode)
}
```

```text
func determineAccessMode(ctx *Base, pkgOwner, doer *user_model.User) (perm.AccessMode, error) {
	if setting.Service.RequireSignInViewStrict && (doer == nil || doer.IsGhost()) {
		return perm.AccessModeNone, nil
	}

	if doer != nil && !doer.IsGhost() && (!doer.IsActive || doer.ProhibitLogin) {
		return perm.AccessModeNone, nil
	}

	// TODO: ActionUser permission check
	accessMode := perm.AccessModeNone
	if pkgOwner.IsOrganization() {
		org := organization.OrgFromUser(pkgOwner)

		if doer != nil && !doer.IsGhost() {
			// 1. If user is logged in, check all team packages permissions
			var err error
			accessMode, err = org.GetOrgUserMaxAuthorizeLevel(ctx, doer.ID)
			if err != nil {
				return accessMode, err
			}
			// If access mode is less than write check every team for more permissions
			// The minimum possible access mode is read for org members
			if accessMode < perm.AccessModeWrite {
				teams, err := organization.GetUserOrgTeams(ctx, org.ID, doer.ID)
				if err != nil {
					return accessMode, err
				}
				for _, t := range teams {
					perm := t.UnitAccessMode(ctx, unit.TypePackages)
					if accessMode < perm {
						accessMode = perm
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if accessMode == perm.AccessModeNone && organization.HasOrgOrUserVisible(ctx, pkgOwner, doer) {
			// 2. If user is unauthorized or no org member, check if org is visible
			accessMode = perm.AccessModeRead
		}
	} else {
		if doer != nil && !doer.IsGhost() {
			// 1. Check if user is package owner
			if doer.ID == pkgOwner.ID {
				accessMode = perm.AccessModeOwner
			} else if pkgOwner.Visibility == structs.VisibleTypePublic || pkgOwner.Visibility == structs.VisibleTypeLimited { // 2. Check if package owner is public or limited
				accessMode = perm.AccessModeRead
			}
		} else if pkgOwner.Visibility == structs.VisibleTypePublic { // 3. Check if package owner is public
			accessMode = perm.AccessModeRead
		}
	}

	return accessMode, nil
}
```

```text
func (opts *StarredReposOptions) ToConds() builder.Cond {
	var cond builder.Cond = builder.Eq{
		"star.uid": opts.StarrerID,
	}
	if opts.RepoOwnerID != 0 {
		cond = cond.And(builder.Eq{
			"repository.owner_id": opts.RepoOwnerID,
		})
	}
	if opts.IncludePrivate {
		// only include private repos the actor can still access, so metadata does not leak after access revocation
		cond = cond.And(AccessibleRepositoryCondition(opts.Actor, unit.TypeInvalid))
	} else {
		// a public repo under a limited/private owner is not publicly reachable, so exclude it too
		cond = cond.And(PublicRepoUnderPublicOwnerCond())
	}
	return cond
}

func (opts *StarredReposOptions) ToJoins() []db.JoinFunc {
	return []db.JoinFunc{
		func(e db.Engine) error {
			e.Join("INNER", "star", "`repository`.id=`star`.repo_id")
			return nil
		},
```

```text
// showUserFeed show user activity as RSS / Atom feed
func showUserFeed(ctx *context.Context, formatType string) {
	includePrivate := ctx.IsSigned && (ctx.Doer.IsAdmin || ctx.Doer.ID == ctx.ContextUser.ID)
	isOrganisation := ctx.ContextUser.IsOrganization()
	if ctx.IsSigned && isOrganisation && !includePrivate {
		// When feed is requested by a member of the organization,
		// include the private repo's the member has access to.
		isOrgMember, err := organization.IsOrganizationMember(ctx, ctx.ContextUser.ID, ctx.Doer.ID)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("IsOrganizationMember", err)
			return
		}
		includePrivate = isOrgMember
	}

	// a public-only API token must not surface private activity, even for its own owner
	if includePrivate && context.TokenIsPublicOnly(ctx) {
		includePrivate = false
	}

	actions, _, err := feed_service.GetFeeds(ctx, activities_model.GetFeedsOptions{
		RequestedUser:   ctx.ContextUser,
		Actor:           ctx.Doer,
		IncludePrivate:  includePrivate,
		OnlyPerformedBy: !isOrganisation,
		IncludeDeleted:  false,
		Date:            ctx.FormString("date"),
	})
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetFeeds", err)
		return
	}
	// - name: page
	//   in: query
	//   description: page number of results to return (1-based)
	//   type: integer
	// - name: limit
	//   in: query
	//   description: page size of results
	//   type: integer
	// responses:
	//   "200":
	//     "$ref": "#/responses/ActivityFeedsList"
	//   "404":
	//     "$ref": "#/responses/notFound"

	includePrivate := false
	if ctx.IsSigned {
		if ctx.Doer.IsAdmin {
			includePrivate = true
		} else {
			org := organization.OrgFromUser(ctx.ContextUser)
			isMember, err := org.IsOrgMember(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID)
			if err != nil {
				ctx.APIErrorInternal(err)
				return
			}
			includePrivate = isMember
		}
	}

	listOptions := utils.GetListOptions(ctx)

	opts := activities_model.GetFeedsOptions{
		RequestedUser:  ctx.ContextUser,
		Actor:          ctx.Doer,
		IncludePrivate: includePrivate,
		Date:           ctx.FormString("date"),
		ListOptions:    listOptions,
	}
	opts.ApplyPublicOnly(ctx.PublicOnly)

	feeds, count, err := feed_service.GetFeeds(ctx, opts)
```

```text
// AddMentionableTeams loads and adds team mentions for the given owner (if it's an org).
func (c *Collector) AddMentionableTeams(ctx context.Context, doer, owner *user_model.User) error {
	if doer == nil || !owner.IsOrganization() {
		return nil
	}

	org := organization.OrgFromUser(owner)
	isAdmin := doer.IsAdmin
	if !isAdmin {
		var err error
		isAdmin, err = org.IsOwnedBy(ctx, doer.ID)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}

	var teams []*organization.Team
	var err error
	if isAdmin {
		teams, err = org.LoadTeams(ctx)
	} else {
		teams, err = org.GetUserTeams(ctx, doer.ID)
	}
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
```

```text
// Settings render the main settings page
func Settings(ctx *context.Context) {
	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("org.settings")
	ctx.Data["PageIsOrgSettings"] = true
	ctx.Data["PageIsSettingsOptions"] = true
	ctx.Data["CurrentVisibility"] = ctx.Org.Organization.Visibility
	ctx.Data["RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess"] = ctx.Org.Organization.RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess
	ctx.Data["ContextUser"] = ctx.ContextUser

	if _, err := shared_user.RenderUserOrgHeader(ctx); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("RenderUserOrgHeader", err)
		return
	}

	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplSettingsOptions)
}

// SettingsPost response for settings change submitted
func SettingsPost(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.UpdateOrgSettingForm)
	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("org.settings")
	ctx.Data["PageIsOrgSettings"] = true
	ctx.Data["PageIsSettingsOptions"] = true
	ctx.Data["CurrentVisibility"] = ctx.Org.Organization.Visibility

	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplSettingsOptions)
		return
	}

	org := ctx.Org.Organization
	if err := org_service.UpdateOrgEmailAddress(ctx, org, form.Email); err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, util.ErrInvalidArgument) {
			ctx.Data["Err_Email"] = true
			ctx.RenderWithErrDeprecated(ctx.Tr("form.email_invalid"), tplSettingsOptions, &form)
			return
		}
		ctx.ServerError("UpdateOrgEmailAddress", err)
		return
	}

	opts := &user_service.UpdateOptions{
		FullName:                  optional.FromPtr(form.FullName),
		Description:               optional.FromPtr(form.Description),
		Website:                   optional.FromPtr(form.Website),
		Location:                  optional.FromPtr(form.Location),
		RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess: optional.FromPtr(form.RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess),
	}
	if ctx.Doer.IsAdmin {
		opts.MaxRepoCreation = optional.FromPtr(form.MaxRepoCreation)
	}

	if err := user_service.UpdateUser(ctx, org.AsUser(), opts); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("UpdateUser", err)
		return
	}

	log.Trace("Organization setting updated: %s", org.Name)
	ctx.Flash.Success(ctx.Tr("org.settings.update_setting_success"))
	ctx.Redirect(ctx.Org.OrgLink + "/settings")
}

// SettingsAvatar response for change avatar on settings page
func SettingsAvatar(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.AvatarForm)
	form.Source = forms.AvatarLocal
	if err := user_setting.UpdateAvatarSetting(ctx, form, ctx.Org.Organization.AsUser()); err != nil {
		ctx.Flash.Error(err.Error())
	} else {
		ctx.Flash.Success(ctx.Tr("org.settings.update_avatar_success"))
	}

	ctx.Redirect(ctx.Org.OrgLink + "/settings")
}

// SettingsDeleteAvatar response for delete avatar on settings page
func SettingsDeleteAvatar(ctx *context.Context) {
	if err := user_service.DeleteAvatar(ctx, ctx.Org.Organization.AsUser()); err != nil {
		ctx.Flash.Error(err.Error())
	}

	ctx.JSONRedirect(ctx.Org.OrgLink + "/settings")
}

// SettingsDeleteOrgPost response for deleting an organization
func SettingsDeleteOrgPost(ctx *context.Context) {
	if ctx.Org.Organization.Name != ctx.FormString("org_name") {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("form.enterred_invalid_org_name"))
		return
}
```

```text
// updateUserWhitelist checks whether the user whitelist changed and returns a whitelist with
// the users from newWhitelist which have write access to the repo.
func updateUserWhitelist(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, currentWhitelist, newWhitelist []int64) (whitelist []int64, err error) {
	hasUsersChanged := !util.SliceSortedEqual(currentWhitelist, newWhitelist)
	if !hasUsersChanged {
		return currentWhitelist, nil
	}

	whitelist = make([]int64, 0, len(newWhitelist))
	for _, userID := range newWhitelist {
		user, err := user_model.GetUserByID(ctx, userID)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetUserByID [user_id: %d, repo_id: %d]: %v", userID, repo.ID, err)
		}
		perm, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, repo, user)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetIndividualUserRepoPermission [user_id: %d, repo_id: %d]: %v", userID, repo.ID, err)
		}

		if !perm.CanWrite(unit.TypeCode) {
			continue // Drop invalid user ID
		}

		whitelist = append(whitelist, userID)
	}

	return whitelist, err
```
```text
}

func filterTrackedTimesByAccess(ctx *context.APIContext, trackedTimes issues_model.TrackedTimeList) (issues_model.TrackedTimeList, error) {
	filtered := make(issues_model.TrackedTimeList, 0, len(trackedTimes))
	for _, trackedTime := range trackedTimes {
		if trackedTime.Issue == nil || trackedTime.Issue.Repo == nil {
			continue
		}
		permission, err := access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(ctx, trackedTime.Issue.Repo, ctx.Doer)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if permission.HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess() {
			filtered = append(filtered, trackedTime)
		}
	}
	return filtered, nil
}
```

```text
// was official on the previous (possibly unprotected) branch would keep satisfying
// the new branch's protection rules.
func RecalculateReviewsOfficial(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue) error {
	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Clearing and restoring the official flags must happen atomically, otherwise a
	// failure in between would leave the reviews without any official flag set.
	return db.WithTx(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		// Only the latest approve/reject review of each reviewer counts as official, so
		// clear the flag on all of them first and restore it only where it still applies.
		if _, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
			Where("issue_id = ?", issue.ID).
			In("type", ReviewTypeApprove, ReviewTypeReject).
			Cols("official").
			Update(&Review{Official: false}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		reviews, err := FindLatestReviews(ctx, FindReviewOptions{
			Types:   []ReviewType{ReviewTypeApprove, ReviewTypeReject},
			IssueID: issue.ID,
		})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
```

The design has holes. One breaks deploy keys outright, and several paths still show private org content to blocked users. Everything below was checked against the code (read-only).

## Ranked problems

**1. Deploy keys are affected: the org itself becomes the blocked "doer". Severity: high (breaks things).**
- **Evidence:**
  - For deploy keys, `routers/private/serv.go:275` sets `results.UserID = repo.OwnerID`, which is the org.
  - That ID becomes the LFS token's user (`cmd/serv.go:271,282`) and the pusher in the hooks.
  - `services/lfs/server.go:599-609` then calls `GetDoerRepoPermission(repo, <org>)`, and so does `hook_pre_receive.go:504-514`.
  - Today the org gets Owner because `user.ID == repo.OwnerID` (`repo_permission.go:438`). Under the design, `HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn(orgID)` is false, so the org is blocked.
- **Result:**
  - Deploy-key LFS over SSH breaks: no uploads, and no downloads from private repos.
  - AGit pushes through a deploy key fail (`hook_pre_receive.go:89`).
  - `-o repo.private` push options fail (`hook_post_receive.go:153-160`).
- **Fix:** `DoerLacksRequiredTwoFactor` should return false when `doer.IsOrganization()` or `doer.ID == org.ID`.

**2. "My own repos" queries skip `AccessibleRepositoryCondition`. Severity: high (leak).**
- **Evidence:** `SearchRepositoryCondition` only adds that condition when `Actor.ID != OwnerID` (`models/repo/repo_list.go:379-381`). Otherwise it builds the list straight from `UserAccessRepoCond`, `UserOrgTeamRepoCond` and `userOrgPublicRepoCondPrivate` (`:429-437`).
- **What leaks:**
  - `GET /api/v1/user/repos` (`routers/api/v1/user/repo.go:111`). Results aren't filtered by permission, so full repo metadata is returned.
  - `/api/v1/repos/search?uid=<self>` and the web `/repo/search?uid=<self>` (`routers/web/repo/repo.go:435`). The dashboard repo list uses the latter (`DashboardRepoList.vue:138`).
  - Dashboard issues and pull requests: the repo IDs are fed to the indexer (`routers/web/user/home.go:459`), so private issue titles appear.
  - The milestones dashboard (`home.go:159-172`).
- **Fix:** put the guard inside the per-user condition helpers (`repo_list.go:278-372`).
  - Express it as `idStr NOT IN (SELECT id FROM repository WHERE owner_id IN <policy orgs>) OR <user has 2FA> OR <user is admin>`, so it doesn't depend on a repository join.
  - `AccessibleRepositoryCondition`, `SearchRepositoryCondition` and `issuePullAccessibleRepoCond` then all inherit it.
  - Also guard `UserAssigned/Mentioned/CreateIssueRepoCond` (`:229-276`). They only check `is_private=false`, so issues in public repos of private orgs still leak.

**3. Notifications and email still deliver private content. Severity: high (leak).**
- **Evidence:**
  - The web notification list filters with `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission(doer)` (`routers/web/user/notification.go:190,298`).
  - The API notification list does the same and returns issue titles (`services/convert/notification.go:30`).
  - Notification creation uses `CheckRepoUnitUser` (`models/activities/notification_list.go:148-151`).
  - Email recipients are chosen the same way (`services/mailer/mail_issue.go:132`, `mail_release.go:57`). Full issue and comment bodies keep arriving by email.
- The design deliberately left these "non-doer" paths alone, but a real non-member would never receive any of this.
- **Fix:** see the alternative under (f). At minimum, enforce inside `CheckRepoUnitUser` (it has no callers that delete data) plus the three list filters.

**4. Creating or transferring repos into the org bypasses all enforcement points. Severity: medium-high (write path).**
- **Evidence:** these paths call `organization.CanCreateOrgRepo` or `GetOrgsCanCreateRepoByUserID` (`org_user.go:106`, `org_list.go:97`) directly:
  - web create and migrate (`routers/web/repo/repo.go:66,101`)
  - web fork into an org (`fork.go:56,182`)
  - API `POST /orgs/{org}/repos` and fork into an org (`api/v1/repo/fork.go:88-113`)
  - API generate from template (`repo.go:399`)
  - API migrate (`migrate.go:90`, uses `IsOwnedBy`)
  - direct transfer (`services/repository/transfer.go:455`) and accepting a transfer (`models/repo/transfer.go:151`)
  - push-to-create (`services/repository/repository.go:77`)
- **Fix:** guard inside `CanCreateOrgRepo` and `GetOrgsCanCreateRepoByUserID`, and at `migrate.go:90`.

**5. `reqUnitAccess` bypasses your `CanReadUnit`/`CanWriteUnit` change. Severity: medium.**
- **Evidence:** `routers/web/web.go:438` calls `Organization.UnitPermission(ctx, ctx.Doer, …)` directly. In public or limited orgs, a blocked member keeps any team Projects-write: they can create, edit and delete org projects, move issues, and use `/mentions-in-owner` (`web.go:1105`, ~1120-1140).
- **Fix:** guard inside `Organization.UnitPermission` (`models/organization/org.go:288`) and drop the nil-doer approach.

**6. Maintainer-edit path. Severity: medium.**
- **Evidence:** `canMaintainerWriteToBranch` checks the doer's base-repo permission with `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission` (`models/issues/pull_list.go:127`).
- **Scenario:** a blocked writer on X/base can still open, web-edit and HTTP-push to a contributor's private fork, which contains X's private code. This goes through `canWriteAsMaintainer` (`services/context/repo.go:442,1105`) and `canWriteCodeRef` in pre-receive (`hook_pre_receive.go:66`).
- **Fix:** use `GetDoerRepoPermission` there.

**7. Smaller doer-facing paths that skip `GetDoerRepoPermission`. Severity: low-medium.**
- `/api/v1/user/times` returns issue titles (`api/v1/repo/issue_tracked_time.go:152,636`).
- The compare page lists branches and tags of the fork's root repo (`routers/web/repo/compare.go:303`).
- The web members page re-checks membership itself (`routers/web/org/members.go:44`), and so does API ListMembers (`api/v1/org/member.go:86`). Blocked users see concealed members.
- `OrgAssignment` searches teams with `UserID=doer` (`services/context/org.go:181-186`), so the user's own private teams still show. Pass 0 when blocked.
- The mention collector uses `IsOwnedBy` (`routers/web/shared/mention/mention.go:59`), exposing all team names.
- `IsUserRepoAdmin` in `services/issue/comments.go:33` (and similar) lets a blocked "admin" bypass user blocks on public repos.
- `convert.ToBranch` reports wrong push/merge flags (`services/convert/convert.go:73-111`).
- API `GetUserOrgsPermissions` still reports `can_create_repository` (`api/v1/org/org.go:180`).

**8. `nonMemberRepoPermission` is stricter than a real non-member for restricted users. Severity: low-medium.**
- **Evidence:** the real code gives restricted users Read on public repos of public orgs when `RequireSignInViewStrict` is off (`access.go:49-52` with `org.go:460`). The proposed formula gives None.
- **Fix:** use `Read iff !repo.IsPrivate && owner.Visibility != Private && (!restricted || (owner.Visibility == Public && !RequireSignInViewStrict))`. Better: factor the "stranger" branch out of `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission` instead of re-deriving it.

**9. Lockout and UX traps. Severity: medium.**
- **Blocked members can't leave the org.** The leave button posts to `/org/{org}/members/action/leave` (`templates/user/settings/organization.tmpl:27`), which requires membership (`web.go:967-969`) and so returns 404. Allow "leave" for blocked members.
- **Some users can never enroll.** When `manage_mfa` is disabled via `USER_DISABLED_FEATURES` or `EXTERNAL_USER_DISABLE_FEATURES` (`user.go:1464`), the enroll handlers return 404 (`2fa.go:160,191`, `webauthn.go:29`). Those users are permanently locked out. Refuse to enable the policy in that case, or at least show a count of affected users.
- **The "owner must have 2FA" check only applies when enabling.** Disabling TOTP (`2fa.go:65-97`), deleting the last WebAuthn key (`webauthn.go:176-187`) or an admin reset (`admin/users.go:452`) silently blocks the user, including the last owner. Re-enrolling fixes it, but warn on the security page and name the affected orgs.

**10. Gating the banner on the session flag misses cases. Severity: low-medium.**
- **Evidence:** the flag is set only at sign-in (`auth.go:124,414`, `oauth.go:434`) and on enrollment (`2fa.go:254`, `webauthn.go:125`). It is never reset when 2FA is removed. It is nil for reverse-proxy and SSPI sessions, so `== false` never matches and the banner never shows.
- **Fix:** set the flag to false on disable or last-credential delete, and treat nil as "unknown, compute it". Also hide the banner on the enroll pages, as `2fa.go:167,199` already does for the site-wide banner.

**11. API `reqOrgVisible` returning 403 contradicts "exactly a non-member". Severity: low.**
- Any non-member gets 200 on `/orgs/{org}/members`, `/public_members` and `/labels` of a public org, but a blocked member would get 403.
- Meanwhile `org.Get` (`api/v1/org/org.go:321`) uses `HasOrgOrUserVisible`, which is still true for a blocked member of a private org.
- **Fix:** apply non-member visibility (404 only for private orgs) in `reqOrgVisible` and `org.Get`. Keep the 403 with message for `reqOrgOwnership`, `reqOrgMembership` and `teamAccessPrivileged`.

**12. SQL details. Severity: low.**
- Write the table as "\`user\`". xorm rewrites backticks per database (as `repo_list.go:389,661` do); a raw `FROM user` fails on PostgreSQL and MSSQL.
- Bind the boolean (`builder.Eq{"require_two_factor": true}`). MSSQL has no `TRUE` literal.
- The columns are `two_factor.uid` and `webauthn_credential.user_id`.
- Add an index on `require_two_factor`.
- Don't reuse `models/user/search.go:152-157` for the compliance count; it only checks TOTP and ignores WebAuthn.

**13. Check order.** `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission` returns before `LoadOwner` for anonymous users on private repos (`repo_permission.go:408-412`). Do the nil, ID≤0, admin and org checks before your new `LoadOwner` call.

**14. Decide on bots, and document what "no rows deleted" leaves open.**
- Bot accounts (`UserTypeBot`, `user.go:65`) would be blocked unless you exempt them.
- Gaps to document:
  - personal forks of private org repos, which the user owns outright
  - deploy keys whose private key the blocked user holds
  - org webhooks pointing at endpoints they control
  - the active stopwatch in the navbar (`routers/common/pagetmpl.go:31`)
  - existing approvals keep their `official` flag and still count toward required approvals

## Answers to (a)–(g)

- **(a)** Covered by #2–#7. These are already fine:
  - through `GetDoerRepoPermission`: attachments, raw files and archives, git HTTP (the anonymous shortcut matches non-member behaviour), and SSH serv skipping the check (only for public, read-only cases).
  - through `AccessibleRepositoryCondition` (once the SQL guard is in): explore, code search, RSS/feeds, heatmap, `/api/v1/repos/issues/search`, and `/orgs/{org}/repos` (filtered per repo).
- **(b)** Non-doer callers of `GetDoerRepoPermission`, apart from the org-as-pusher cases in #1:
  - automerge (`services/automerge/automerge.go:248`): a blocked scheduler's merge just doesn't fire and the row is kept.
  - `ifNeedApproval` (`notifier_helper.go:469`): fork-PR runs from blocked authors need approval.
  - `services/pull/pull.go:84,170`: the poster is the doer here.
  - webhook/actions payload `permissions`: cosmetic only.
  - None of them delete rows.
- **(c)** Nothing caches permissions across requests. `RepoUserPermission` (`convert/pull.go:64`) and `convert/issue.go:244` are per-request. The request cache comes from `ProtocolMiddlewares` on the root router (`routers/init.go:179` → `middleware.go:91`), which wraps `/api/internal` (serv, hooks), git HTTP and LFS. Queue and cron jobs have no cache and fall through to the DB. The only stale state is the session flag (#10).
- **(d)** See #12.
- **(e)** See #9.
- **(f)** Putting the check in `HasOrgOrUserVisible` + `accessLevel` would be worse:
  - `HasOrgOrUserVisible` returns true for public and limited orgs before it ever checks membership (`org.go:460`).
  - Team unit permissions (`repo_permission.go:461-494`) never go through `accessLevel`.
  - `accessLevel` feeds `IsUserRepoAdmin` at `services/repository/create.go:429`, which would insert an admin collaborator row.

  **Simpler and fail-closed:** enforce in `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`, and give these few callers an explicit "ignore policy" variant because they write or delete based on the result:
  - `services/repository/collaboration.go:103,116` (Reconsider*)
  - `repo_team.go:113,194`
  - `transfer.go:466`, which could downgrade a collaborator to Read
  - `models/git/protected_branch.go:539`, which drops users from the whitelist
  - `models/issues/review.go:292` via `RecalculateReviewsOfficial`, which clears `official`

  That closes #3, #6, #7 and the whole `CheckRepoUnitUser`/`HasAccessUnit`/`AccessLevel` family in one place, and `GetDoerRepoPermission` needs no change. Add the SQL helper guard (#2), `UnitPermission` (#5), `CanCreateOrgRepo` (#4), `OrgAssignment` and the API guards. The cost: while blocked, users aren't mentioned, assigned, notified or given feed entries. Nothing is deleted.
- **(g)** With the policy off, every guard exits on an in-memory flag, so existing org and team tests should pass. Watch for:
  - Swagger needs regenerating if the field is added to the API types.
  - Always write the plain bool (`optional.Some`). The existing `*bool` for `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess` (`services/forms/org.go:45` + `optional.FromPtr`) can't be unchecked, so your choice is correct.
  - Put the "owner has 2FA" validation in `services/user/update.go`, not only in the web handler, so the API can't skip it.
  - In fixtures, only user 24 (TOTP) and user 32 (WebAuthn) are enrolled.

## What I'd cut
- **The 403 in `reqOrgVisible`:** replace it with non-member semantics (#11).
- **The nil-doer change in `CanReadUnit`/`CanWriteUnit` and the separate `issue_search.go` patch:** unnecessary once the guard lives in `UnitPermission` and the SQL helpers.
- **`ctx.Org.TwoFactorBlocked`:** private orgs return 404 before any template sees it, and the global banner covers the UX. Keep it only if you'll show a notice on public org pages.
- **The per-collaborator 2FA label on the repo collaborators page:** replace it with one count ("N members, M outside collaborators without 2FA") on the org settings page. The members page already shows a 2FA column to owners (`members.tmpl:40-43`).

```text
type Access struct {
	ID     int64 `xorm:"pk autoincr"`
	UserID int64 `xorm:"UNIQUE(s)"`
	RepoID int64 `xorm:"UNIQUE(s)"`
	Mode   perm.AccessMode
}

func init() {
	db.RegisterModel(new(Access))
}

func accessLevel(ctx context.Context, user *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository) (perm.AccessMode, error) {
	mode := perm.AccessModeNone
	var userID int64
	restricted := false

	if user != nil {
		userID = user.ID
		restricted = user.IsRestricted
	}

	if err := repo.LoadOwner(ctx); err != nil {
		return mode, err
	}

	repoIsFullyPublic := !setting.Service.RequireSignInViewStrict && repo.Owner.Visibility == structs.VisibleTypePublic && !repo.IsPrivate
	if (restricted && repoIsFullyPublic) || (!restricted && !repo.IsPrivate) {
		mode = perm.AccessModeRead
	}

	if userID == 0 {
		return mode, nil
	}

	if userID == repo.OwnerID {
		return perm.AccessModeOwner, nil
	}

	a, exist, err := db.Get[Access](ctx, builder.Eq{"user_id": userID, "repo_id": repo.ID})
	if err != nil {
		return mode, err
	} else if !exist {
		return mode, nil
	}
	return a.Mode, nil
}
```

```markdown
# Plan — Issue #35: Require two-factor authentication for an organization's members

## Context

Issue #35 (owner: @Jack-Donohue, Sprint 1 milestone) asks for an org-level policy: an owner can require 2FA
for everyone with access to the org's code. Today 2FA is opt-in per user. The only enforcement is the
site-wide `[security] TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = enforced` setting, and it is only checked in web `RepoAssignment`
(services/context/repo.go:432) and API `repoAssignment` (routers/api/v1/api.go:197). Git HTTP, SSH, LFS,
packages and listings all ignore it, which is exactly the "scattered checks leave gaps" failure the issue
warns about.

The issue asks for:
1. a policy flag plus a migration,
2. a compliance view,
3. enforcement in the shared permission layer, with the API-path test written first,
4. a deliberate decision on what happens to non-compliant members,
5. a per-request cache of the 2FA answer.

**Decisions**
- **Coverage** (user's choice): org members **and** outside collaborators on the org's repos.
  - Site admins are exempt.
  - Only individual and bot accounts are covered. Org identities are exempt, because deploy-key pushes
    run as the org (routers/private/serv.go:275). Actions task users and the ghost user (ID ≤ 0) are
    exempt too.
- **Non-compliant users** (user: "stay within the issue's requests"; recommended here, override if
  wanted): **reversible lockout**.
  - A covered user without TOTP or a passkey is treated **exactly as a signed-in non-member**.
  - Enrolling restores access on the next request.
  - Nothing is deleted or changed in the database.
- **Out of scope** (not requested by the issue): the policy on the org-create form, a REST API field and
  swagger change, a grace period, emailing non-compliant users, blocking 2FA removal for org members,
  and letting blocked members leave the org.

## Step 0 — branch and spec (D2/D3, before any code)

- `git switch main && git pull origin main && git switch -c feat/issue-35-require-org-2fa`. Local main is
  24 commits behind; none of them touch these files. Migration **v344** is free on every branch.
- Add `drafts-issue-35/` to `.git/info/exclude`, as was done for drafts-issue-34.
- Write `drafts-issue-35/issue-35-spec.md` in the COURSE-WORKFLOW user-story format:
  - User Story and Scenario.
  - ACs below.
  - Out of Scope (list above).
  - Open Questions: None.
  - Design Decisions 1–3 below.
  - Scope: the label is `scope: medium`. I'd suggest `large` given the touch points; the team decides.
- Jack posts the spec and asks a teammate for a "Spec reviewed" comment.

**Acceptance criteria (draft)**
1. With 2FA enrolled, an owner ticks **Require two-factor authentication** in Org Settings and saves. The
   setting is stored and shown checked. Unticking and saving turns it off.
2. An owner without 2FA who is not a site admin can't enable it. They get an error telling them to enrol
   first, and the policy stays off.
3. With the policy on, a member or outside collaborator without 2FA gets on a **private** org repo,
   through web, API token, git over HTTP, SSH and LFS, exactly what a signed-in non-member gets (404 /
   denied). On a **public** org repo they can only read: no push, no write.
4. That user gets 404 on member-only org web pages (teams, settings, private org's pages). Member- or
   owner-only org API endpoints return **403** with "organization requires two-factor authentication".
   They can't create, fork, migrate or transfer repos into the org, or upload org packages.
5. That user's repo lists, search, dashboard issue and PR lists, feeds, notifications and emails no longer
   include the org's private repos or their issues.
6. After enrolling TOTP or a passkey, the next request restores all previous access. No membership, team,
   collaborator, assignee, watch, whitelist or review row changed while they were blocked.
7. That user sees a banner on every page saying an organization they belong to requires 2FA, with a link
   to enrol. It is hidden on the enrol pages.
8. Compliance view, when the policy is on:
   - the Members page shows owners how many members lack 2FA and flags each one as having no access;
   - the Settings page shows counts of members and outside collaborators without 2FA;
   - a repo's Collaborators settings page flags collaborators without 2FA.
9. Site admins, deploy keys and Actions tokens are unaffected.
10. With the policy off (the default for every org, including after the upgrade), behaviour is unchanged.

**Design Decision 1 — where it is enforced.**
- **Decision:** fail-closed inside `access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`, with SQL twins in the
  per-user repo conditions and guards on the org-membership checks. Callers that write or delete based on
  the result opt out explicitly.
- **Alternatives Considered:**
  - (a) Per-handler checks, as the site-wide setting does. This misses git, SSH and LFS.
  - (b) Only `GetDoerRepoPermission`. This misses notifications, email, maintainer edits and ~40 direct
    callers.
- **Consequence:** blocked users disappear from assignee, reviewer and mention candidate lists, and get
  no notifications, mail or feed rows while blocked.

**Design Decision 2 — what happens to non-compliant users.**
- **Decision:** reversible lockout as a non-member.
- **Alternatives Considered:**
  - read-only: secrets stay readable, which is the very risk the issue names;
  - grace period: needs an "enforced since" column and a countdown;
  - removal, as GitHub does: destroys team and collaborator setup.
- **Consequences:**
  - The lockout is immediate, so the settings page shows counts before enabling, and the owner must have
    2FA.
  - An owner who later removes 2FA locks themselves out; another owner or a site admin can recover.
  - Blocked members can't leave until they enrol.
  - Users barred from managing 2FA (`manage_mfa` disabled) can't comply.

**Design Decision 3 — storage.**
- **Decision:** a `require_two_factor` column on `user`, next to `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess`.
- **Alternatives Considered:** a `user_setting` key/value row.
- **Rationale:** `repo.Owner` is already loaded on the permission path, so a disabled policy costs no
  extra query, and the SQL conditions can select policy orgs directly.

## Implementation (TDD order: the API-path test is written first)

**1. Schema**
- `models/user/user.go`: add `RequireTwoFactor bool \`xorm:"NOT NULL DEFAULT false INDEX"\`` in the
  "For organization" block (~147).
- `models/migrations/v1_27/v344.go`, `AddRequireTwoFactorToUser`:
  - local struct, `SyncWithOptions{IgnoreDropIndices, IgnoreConstrains}`, copied from v343;
  - register it in `models/migrations/migrations.go` after line 423;
  - add `v344_test.go` plus `fixtures/Test_AddRequireTwoFactorToUser/user.yml`, with a blank import of
    `gitea.dev/models/user`.

**2. Write first:** `tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go`, API subtests (see Verification). Confirm
they fail.

**3. Policy primitive**
- New `models/organization/org_two_factor.go`: `func (org *Organization) DoerLacksRequiredTwoFactor(ctx,
  doer) (bool, error)`.
  - Returns false when the policy is off, the doer is nil, not individual or bot, or a site admin.
  - Otherwise returns `!has`, where `has` comes from
    `cache.GetWithContextCache(ctx, cachegroup.UserHasTwoFactor, doer.ID, auth_model.HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn)`
    (modules/cache/context.go:38). The request cache is set for all routes, including internal serv,
    git and LFS (routers/common/middleware.go:91).
  - Add `UserHasTwoFactor` to `modules/cachegroup`.
- Count helpers for the compliance view:
  - `CountOrgMembersWithoutTwoFactor`, `CountOrgOutsideCollaboratorsWithoutTwoFactor`.
  - Both check TOTP **and** WebAuthn. Don't reuse `models/user/search.go:152`, which checks TOTP only.
- New `models/user/two_factor_policy.go` with SQL helpers:
  - `RequireTwoFactorOrgIDs()`: `` SELECT id FROM `user` WHERE require_two_factor = ? ``, with the bool
    bound;
  - `TwoFactorPolicyMetCond(userID)`: the user is an admin, or has a `two_factor.uid` or
    `webauthn_credential.user_id` row.
  - Quote `` `user` `` as the existing conditions do (repo_list.go:389).

**4. Repo permission layer** (`models/perm/access/repo_permission.go`)
- In `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`, after the nil-user returns and `LoadOwner`, before the visibility
  check:
  - if the owner is an org and `DoerLacksRequiredTwoFactor`, return the **non-member** permission;
  - the deferred `finalProcessRepoUnitPermission` still applies everyone and anonymous unit modes.
- Non-member mode is computed by factoring the "stranger" logic out of the existing code, not re-derived:
  - visibility as for a non-member: add `organization.HasOrgOrUserVisibleToNonMember`, split out of
    `HasOrgOrUserVisible` (org.go:449);
  - the public part of `accessLevel` (access.go:49-52), which keeps the restricted-user and
    `RequireSignInViewStrict` rules;
  - no collaborator, `access` table or team modes.
- Add the same guard to `IsUserRepoAdmin` and `IsUserRealRepoAdmin`, which don't go through the function
  above.
- Opt-out: `access_model.IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy(ctx) context.Context`, a context marker checked by the
  guard. Wrap these bookkeeping callers, each with a one-line why-comment:
  - `services/repository/collaboration.go:103,116`
  - `services/repository/repo_team.go:113,194`
  - `services/repository/transfer.go:466`
  - `models/git/protected_branch.go:539`
  - `models/issues/review.go:292`
- `GetDoerRepoPermission` is unchanged. This covers web, API, git HTTP, SSH serv, pre-receive, LFS,
  notifications, mail, maintainer edits, and the `CheckRepoUnitUser` / `HasAccessUnit` / `CanBeAssigned`
  family.

**5. SQL twin** (`models/repo/repo_list.go:229-372`)
- AND `(TwoFactorPolicyMetCond(uid) OR idStr NOT IN (SELECT id FROM repository WHERE owner_id IN
  RequireTwoFactorOrgIDs()))` into each per-user helper:
  - `UserAccessRepoCond`, `UserCollaborationRepoCond`, `UserOrgTeamRepoCond`, `userOrgTeamUnitRepoCond`,
    `UserOrgUnitRepoCond`;
  - `userOrgPublicRepoCond`, `userOrgPublicRepoCondPrivate`, `UserOrgPublicUnitRepoCond`;
  - `UserAssigned/Mentioned/CreateIssueRepoCond`.
- Then `AccessibleRepositoryCondition`, `SearchRepositoryCondition`'s "my repos" branch (:429) and
  `issuePullAccessibleRepoCond` all inherit it, and so do `/api/v1/user/repos`, the dashboard, indexer
  repo-ID lists, feeds and code search. Clause 1 (public repos) is untouched, so non-member parity holds.

**6. Org-level guards** (each one: "blocked ⇒ behave as non-member")
- **Model layer:**
  - `Organization.UnitPermission` (org.go:288): ignore teams when blocked. This covers `reqUnitAccess`
    (web.go:438) and `CanRead/WriteUnit`.
  - `CanCreateOrgRepo` (org_user.go:106) and `GetOrgsCanCreateRepoByUserID` (org_list.go:97): add the SQL
    policy guard. This covers create, fork, migrate, generate, transfer and push-to-create.
- **Web** — `services/context/org.go` `OrgAssignment`:
  - after the non-admin `IsOwner`/`IsMember` lookup, when blocked, clear
    IsOwner/IsMember/IsTeamMember/IsTeamAdmin/CanCreateOrgRepo;
  - skip the `IsTeamMember` recompute;
  - search teams with `UserID: 0`.
  - `routers/web/org/members.go:44`: use `ctx.Org.IsMember` instead of re-querying.
- **API** — one helper in routers/api/v1/api.go:
  - `reqOrgOwnership`, `reqOrgMembership` and `teamAccessPrivileged` return 403 with a message;
  - `reqOrgVisible` and `org.Get` (api/v1/org/org.go:321) use the non-member visibility, so 404 only for
    private orgs;
  - `api/v1/org/member.go:86` and `repo/migrate.go:90` (`IsOwnedBy`) get the same guard.
- **Packages** — `services/context/package.go` `determineAccessMode` (~113): when blocked, skip team modes
  and use the non-member visibility.
- **Smaller doer paths:** `routers/web/shared/mention/mention.go:59` and `api/v1/org/org.go:180`
  (`can_create_repository`).

**7. Settings, compliance view, banner**
- Settings:
  - `services/forms/org.go` `UpdateOrgSettingForm`: add `RequireTwoFactor bool` as a plain bool written
    with `optional.Some`. The existing `*bool` pattern can't save "unchecked".
  - `services/user/update.go` `UpdateOptions`: add `RequireTwoFactor` and the column.
  - `routers/web/org/setting.go` `Settings` / `SettingsPost`: if enabling, the doer is not admin and has
    no 2FA, re-render with an error. Pass the two counts to the template.
  - `templates/org/settings/options.tmpl`: checkbox plus help text and counts.
- Members page (`routers/web/org/members.go:78`, `templates/org/member/members.tmpl:40`):
  `RequireTwoFactor` and the count go to the template; when the policy is on, show a summary line and a
  "no access until 2FA" label next to ✗.
- Collaborators page (`routers/web/repo/setting/collaboration.go:28`, `collaboration.tmpl`): for org repos
  with the policy on, add a 2FA label via `UserList.GetTwoFaStatus`.
- Banner:
  - `services/context/context.go` (~203) sets `ShowOrgTwoFactorRequiredMessage` unless the session's
    `KeyUserHasTwoFactorAuth` is `true`;
  - it uses one EXISTS query for "member of, or collaborator on a repo of, a policy org", then the cached
    2FA check;
  - render it in `templates/base/alert.tmpl` beside the site-wide banner, hidden on the enrol pages
    (2fa.go:167,199);
  - set the session flag to false on TOTP disable (`security/2fa.go` `DisableTwoFactor`) and on deleting
    the last passkey (`security/webauthn.go` `WebauthnDelete`).
- Locale: new `org.settings.require_two_factor*`, `org.members.two_factor_*` and `auth.org_twofa_required`
  keys in `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` only.

**8. Context docs (AGENTS.md rule)**
- `.claude-students/docs/models-user-org-perm.md`:
  - the policy, its enforcement points, and the `IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy` rule for bookkeeping code;
  - the fork has `GetDoerRepoPermission` / `GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`.
- `docs/testing.md`: `loginUser` can't pass TOTP, so log in first, then insert the `TwoFactor` row.
- Regenerate both `guide/` twins and run `./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Verification

**Unit tests**
- `models/organization/org_two_factor_test.go`:
  - `DoerLacksRequiredTwoFactor` for: policy off; on with user4 (no 2FA) → true; user1 admin, user24

- `models/perm/access/repo_permission_test.go` `TestRepoPermissionTwoFactorPolicy`:
  - user4 (org3 team1, write) on repo3 (private) → none;
  - on repo32 (public) → equal to stranger user5's permission, including a restricted variant;
  - an outside collaborator → none;
  - after inserting a TOTP row → write restored;
  - admin, and org-as-doer (deploy key) → owner;
  - `IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy` → real permission;
  - `IsUserRepoAdmin` guarded.

  ./models/migrations/v1_27/`).

**Integration** — `tests/integration/org_two_factor_test.go`, one test with subtests, under 2s:
- Enable the policy on org3 with `user_model.UpdateUserCols`.
- Enrol by inserting a `TwoFactor` row (pattern at auth_oauth2_test.go:532) after login.
- Subtests:
  - **API (first):** user4 token on `/api/v1/repos/org3/repo3` gives 200, then 404 when blocked, then
    200 after enrolment. `/api/v1/orgs/org3/teams` gives 403 with the message. `/api/v1/repos/org3/repo21`
    has `permissions.push=false`. `/api/v1/user/repos` and `/api/v1/repos/issues/search` exclude org3's
    private repos.
  - **git HTTP:** token basic auth on `/org3/repo3.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack` is denied, and
    receive-pack on repo21 is denied.
  - **SSH:** extend `tests/integration/api_private_serv_test.go` with `private.ServCommand` for user4's
    key on org3/repo3 (denied when blocked) and an org3 deploy key (still allowed).
  - **Web:** `/org3/repo3` and `/org/org3/teams` return 404; the banner shows on `/`.
  - **Settings:** user2 without 2FA can't enable the policy; after a TOTP row they can; unticking saves
    false. The members page shows the count and label.
  - **Packages:** user2's generic upload to org3 is denied when blocked.
- Run `make 'test-integration#TestOrgTwoFactor'` and `make 'test-integration#TestAPIPrivateServ'`.

**Regression**
- `go test ./models/perm/access/ ./models/repo/ ./models/organization/ ./models/issues/
  ./services/context/ ./services/repository/...`
- Integration org/team/collaborator/fork/transfer suites, e.g.
  `-run '^(TestOrg.*|TestAPIOrg.*|TestAPITeam.*|TestAPIRepoCollaborator.*|TestRepoFork.*|TestAPIRepoTransfer.*|TestAPIPrivateServ)$'`.
  The policy defaults to off, so these must pass unchanged.

**Lint and manual check**
- `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `make lint-templates`, `./.claude-students/check.sh`.
- Run the binary by hand: org3 with the policy on, user4 sees the banner, gets 404 on repo3 and can't
  clone it; enrolling TOTP restores access.
```

The plan is ready to review. Some things changed from the issue's framing, and you should know them before approving:

- **The issue hinted at the wrong place for the check.** A second review found that a check only on the signed-in user's own requests misses several leaks. "My repos" lists, the dashboard, notifications and emails would all still expose private org content. The plan makes the check fail-closed in the main per-user permission function instead. The few spots that change or delete data based on that result (unassigning issues, dropping watches, editing branch-protection lists, recounting official reviews, transfers) opt out explicitly. Otherwise a blocked user would lose those rows for good.
- **Deploy keys had to be exempted.** Deploy-key pushes run as the organization itself, which never has 2FA, so a naive check would have broken them.
- **What I decided for non-compliant members:** you asked me to stay within the issue rather than pick, so I recommended a reversible lockout. Members and outside collaborators without 2FA are treated as non-members until they enrol, and nothing is deleted. The other two options are in the spec's Design Decision. Read-only leaves secrets readable, which is the risk the issue names. A grace period needs extra schema. Change this if you prefer one of those.
- **The compliance view mostly existed already.** The org Members page already shows owners each member's 2FA status. The plan adds counts, labels and the collaborator side.
- **Scope label:** the work touches many files. I'd suggest relabelling the issue `scope: large`, but that's for the team to decide.
- **A probable bug, not fixed here:** the existing "Repository admin can add and remove access for teams" checkbox probably can't be unchecked from the web form. I haven't confirmed it, so the plan suggests filing it as a separate bug issue.

```text
  - grace period: needs an "enforced since" column and a countdown;
  - removal, as GitHub does: destroys team and collaborator setup.
- **Consequences:**
  - The lockout is immediate, so the settings page shows counts before enabling, and the owner must have
    2FA.
  - An owner who later removes 2FA locks themselves out; another owner or a site admin can recover.
  - Blocked members can't leave until they enrol.
  - Users barred from managing 2FA (`manage_mfa` disabled) can't comply.

**Design Decision 3 — storage.**
- **Decision:** a `require_two_factor` column on `user`, next to `RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess`.
- **Alternatives Considered:** a `user_setting` key/value row.
- **Rationale:** `repo.Owner` is already loaded on the permission path, so a disabled policy costs no
  extra query, and the SQL conditions can select policy orgs directly.

they fail.
```

```markdown
Suggested new title: Require two-factor authentication for an organization's members and collaborators

## User Story
As an organization owner, I want to require two-factor authentication for everyone with access to my organization's code so that one member's reused [REDACTED:generic-[REDACTED:generic-password]] cannot expose our private repositories, packages and secrets.

## User Scenario
Priya owns the `acme` organization, which has private repositories, a container package and Actions secrets. She already uses an authenticator app. She opens **Settings** for `acme` and sees a new **Require two-factor authentication** checkbox. Under it, a note says "3 members and 1 outside collaborator have not enabled two-factor authentication and will lose access until they do". She opens the **Members** page: as an owner she sees a 2FA column, and the three members without it are marked "No access until 2FA is enabled". She posts in the team chat, waits a day, then ticks the box and saves.

Sam, one of the three, never enrolled. On his next page load a banner says an organization he belongs to requires two-factor authentication and links to the enrolment page. Until he enrols, Gitea treats him as if he were not in `acme`:
- `acme`'s private repositories return 404 in the browser and the API;
- `git clone` and `git push` over HTTPS or SSH are refused;
- the private repositories and their issues disappear from his dashboard, search results and notifications;
- he can still read `acme`'s public repositories, like anyone else.

Sam scans the QR code and enters a code. His next request has his old access back, his team memberships and issue assignments untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given an owner of an organization who has two-factor authentication (TOTP or a passkey), when they tick **Require two-factor authentication** in the organization's settings and save, then the setting is stored and the page shows it ticked. Unticking it and saving turns the policy off.
- [ ] AC2: Given an owner who has no two-factor authentication and is not a site administrator, when they try to turn the policy on, then the save is refused with a message telling them to enable two-factor authentication on their own account first, and the policy stays off.
- [ ] AC3: Given the policy is on and a member or outside collaborator who has neither TOTP nor a passkey, when they open a private repository of the organization in the browser, through the API with a token, with git over HTTP or SSH, or through LFS, then they get exactly what a signed-in non-member gets (404 or access denied). On the organization's public repositories they can read but not push or write.
- [ ] AC4: Given the same user, when they open member-only organization pages (teams, settings, any page of a private organization), then they get 404 as a non-member would. When they call member-only or owner-only organization API endpoints, they get 403 with a message saying the organization requires two-factor authentication. They cannot create, fork, migrate or transfer repositories into the organization or upload packages to it.
- [ ] AC5: Given the same user, then their repository lists, repository search, dashboard issue and pull request lists, activity feeds, notifications and emails no longer include the organization's private repositories or their issues and pull requests.
- [ ] AC6: Given the same user, when they enrol in TOTP or register a passkey, then their next request has all their previous access back. No organization membership, team membership, collaborator, assignee, watch, branch-protection allowlist or review row was removed or changed while they were blocked.
- [ ] AC7: Given the same user, when they load any page except the two-factor enrolment pages, then a banner tells them an organization they belong to requires two-factor authentication and links to the enrolment page.
- [ ] AC8: Given the policy is on, when an owner opens the organization's **Members** page, then they see how many members have not enabled two-factor authentication, and each such member is marked as having no access until they do. The **Settings** page shows the number of members and outside collaborators without two-factor authentication. A repository's **Collaborators** settings page marks each collaborator without it.
- [ ] AC9: Given the policy is on, then site administrators, deploy keys and Actions tokens keep the access they had before.
- [ ] AC10: Given an organization that has never turned the policy on (every organization after the upgrade), then nothing about access or the UI changes for it.

## Out of Scope
- Setting the policy when the organization is created, and a field for it in the REST API (`/api/v1/orgs`).
- A grace period before the lockout starts.
- Emailing members who have not enrolled.
- Stopping a member of such an organization from disabling their own two-factor authentication.
- Letting a blocked member leave the organization before they enrol (an owner can still remove them).
- The site-wide `[security] TWO_FACTOR_AUTH = enforced` setting, which keeps working as it does today.
- Translations other than en-US (handled by the project's translation process).

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1
**Decision:** Enforce the policy inside the shared permission function `access_model.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission`, fail-closed, plus the matching SQL conditions used for repository lists and searches and the organization membership checks. The few callers that write or delete rows based on a user's permission (re-checking assignees and watches after access changes, saving a branch-protection allowlist, recounting official reviews, repository transfer) opt out explicitly.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Checks in individual handlers, the way the site-wide 2FA setting works today. It is only checked in the web and API repository middleware, so git over HTTP and SSH, LFS, packages and every listing ignore it. (b) A check only in `GetDoerRepoPermission`, the entry point for the signed-in user's own requests. Notifications, emails, maintainer edits and about forty other callers bypass it.
**Rationale:** Every access path already goes through the permission function or the listing conditions, so one check there covers web, API, git HTTP, SSH, LFS, notifications and email at once. Paths added later get it by default instead of leaking by default.
**Consequences:** While blocked, a user is no longer offered as an assignee, reviewer or @mention, and gets no notifications, emails or feed entries for the organization's private repositories. Code that writes or deletes rows based on permission must remember to opt out; the opt-out is a named helper so reviewers can grep for it. Repository list queries gain one extra condition, which is cheap when no organization uses the policy.

### Decision 2
**Decision:** A member or outside collaborator without two-factor authentication is treated exactly as a signed-in non-member of the organization until they enrol. This is a reversible lockout: nothing is deleted.
**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Read-only access: the private code and secrets stay readable, which is the risk this issue exists to remove. (b) A grace period: needs an "enforced since" date, a countdown in the UI and time-based tests. (c) Removing the user from the organization, as GitHub does: it destroys their team and collaborator setup, which an owner then has to rebuild.
**Rationale:** It is the most secure option, it is undone simply by enrolling, and "non-member" is a behaviour the permission code already defines, so the blocked case reuses it instead of inventing a new access level.
**Consequences:** The lockout takes effect the moment the box is saved. That is why the settings page shows who will be affected, and why an owner must have two-factor authentication before turning it on. An owner who later removes their own two-factor authentication locks themselves out too; another owner or a site administrator can turn the policy off. A blocked member cannot leave the organization until they enrol. Users whose instance does not allow them to manage two-factor authentication cannot comply.

### Decision 3
**Decision:** Store the policy as a `require_two_factor` column on the `user` table, which also holds organizations, next to the existing `repo_admin_change_team_access` organization setting.
**Alternatives Considered:** A key/value row in the `user_setting` table, which needs no new column.
**Rationale:** The permission code already loads the repository owner's row, so checking the flag costs no extra query when the policy is off. The SQL conditions for lists and searches can also select the organizations that require two-factor authentication directly.
**Consequences:** It needs a database migration and an index on a wide, heavily used table.

## Scope
medium (`scope: medium`) as originally estimated. One setting and one compliance view, but enforcement touches the permission layer, the listing queries and the organization membership checks. `scope: large` may be the more honest label.
```

```bash
- `git clone` and `git push` over HTTPS or SSH are refused;
- the private repositories and their issues disappear from Sam's dashboard, search results and notifications;
- Sam can still read `acme`'s public repositories, like anyone else.

Sam scans the QR code and enters a code. The next request has Sam's old access back, with team memberships and issue assignments untouched.

'''
```

How the draft answers each point:

| Review point | Where it's answered |
|---|---|

| User Scenario | An owner turns the policy on; a member without 2FA is locked out, sees a banner, enrols, and gets their access back |

| Open Questions | None |
| What happens to existing non-compliant members | **Decision 1** (moved to the top so it's the first thing the reviewer sees) |

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package integration

import (
	"net/http"
	"testing"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	api "gitea.dev/modules/structs"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func setOrgRequireTwoFactor(t *testing.T, orgName string, require2FA bool) {
	org := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{Name: orgName})
	org.RequireTwoFactor = require2FA
	require.NoError(t, user_model.UpdateUserCols(t.Context(), org, "require_two_factor"))
}

// enrolTOTP gives the user a TOTP device directly, so an already signed-in session or token keeps working
func enrolTOTP(t *testing.T, userName string) {
	u := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{Name: userName})
	tfa := &auth_model.TwoFactor{UID: u.ID}
	require.NoError(t, tfa.SetSecret("JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP"))
	require.NoError(t, auth_model.NewTwoFactor(t.Context(), tfa))
}

func repoFullNames(repos []*api.Repository) []string {
	names := make([]string, 0, len(repos))
	for _, r := range repos {
		names = append(names, r.FullName)
	}
	return names
}

// org3 fixtures: user4 is a member with write on private repo3 through team1, and user10 is an
// outside collaborator with write on public repo21. Neither has 2FA.
func TestOrgTwoFactorPolicy(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()

	t.Run("API", func(t *testing.T) {
		defer tests.PrintCurrentTest(t)()
		defer setOrgRequireTwoFactor(t, "org3", false)

		user4Token := getUserToken(t, "user4", auth_model.AccessTokenScopeReadRepository, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeReadOrganization,
			auth_model.AccessTokenScopeReadUser, auth_model.AccessTokenScopeReadIssue)
		user10Token := getUserToken(t, "user10", auth_model.AccessTokenScopeReadRepository)

		getRepo := func(token, repo string, expectedStatus int) *api.Repository {
			resp := MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/repos/org3/"+repo).AddTokenAuth(token), expectedStatus)
			if expectedStatus != http.StatusOK {
				return nil
			}
			return DecodeJSON(t, resp, &api.Repository{})
		}
		listMyRepos := func() []string {
			resp := MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/user/repos").AddTokenAuth(user4Token), http.StatusOK)
			return repoFullNames(DecodeJSON(t, resp, []*api.Repository{}))
		}
		searchIssueIDs := func() []int64 {
			resp := MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/repos/issues/search?state=all&type=issues").AddTokenAuth(user4Token), http.StatusOK)
			var ids []int64
			for _, issue := range DecodeJSON(t, resp, []*api.Issue{}) {
				ids = append(ids, issue.ID)
			}
			return ids
		}

		// before the policy: ordinary member and collaborator access
		getRepo(user4Token, "repo3", http.StatusOK)
		assert.True(t, getRepo(user10Token, "repo21", http.StatusOK).Permissions.Push)
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/orgs/org3/teams").AddTokenAuth(user4Token), http.StatusOK)
		assert.Contains(t, listMyRepos(), "org3/repo3")
		assert.Contains(t, searchIssueIDs(), int64(6)) // issue6 lives in org3/repo3

		setOrgRequireTwoFactor(t, "org3", true)

		// blocked: exactly what a signed-in non-member gets
		getRepo(user4Token, "repo3", http.StatusNotFound)
		repo21 := getRepo(user10Token, "repo21", http.StatusOK)
		assert.True(t, repo21.Permissions.Pull)
		assert.False(t, repo21.Permissions.Push)
		resp := MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/orgs/org3/teams").AddTokenAuth(user4Token), http.StatusForbidden)
		assert.Contains(t, resp.Body.String(), "requires two-factor authentication")
		assert.NotContains(t, listMyRepos(), "org3/repo3")
		assert.NotContains(t, searchIssueIDs(), int64(6))

		// enrolling restores access on the next request; nothing was removed meanwhile
		enrolTOTP(t, "user4")
		getRepo(user4Token, "repo3", http.StatusOK)
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/api/v1/orgs/org3/teams").AddTokenAuth(user4Token), http.StatusOK)
		assert.Contains(t, listMyRepos(), "org3/repo3")
		assert.Contains(t, searchIssueIDs(), int64(6))
	})
}
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package user

import "xorm.io/builder"

// RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder selects the IDs of the organizations that require two-factor authentication.
func RequireTwoFactorOrgIDsBuilder() *builder.Builder {
	return builder.Select("`user`.id").From("`user`").Where(builder.Eq{"`user`.require_two_factor": true})
}

// HasTwoFactorCond matches rows whose userIDCol (e.g. "`org_user`.uid") is a user enrolled in TOTP or WebAuthn.
func HasTwoFactorCond(userIDCol string) builder.Cond {
	return builder.Or(
		builder.In(userIDCol, builder.Select("uid").From("two_factor")),
		builder.In(userIDCol, builder.Select("user_id").From("webauthn_credential")),
	)
}

// TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond is the SQL twin of organization.IsTwoFactorBlocked: it is true when no
// organization's two-factor policy can block the user, because they are a site admin, not a person
// (an organization pushing through a deploy key) or enrolled in TOTP or WebAuthn.
func TwoFactorPolicyExemptCond(userID int64) builder.Cond {
	return builder.Or(
		builder.Exists(builder.Select("`user`.id").From("`user`").Where(builder.Eq{"`user`.id": userID}.And(builder.Or(
			builder.Eq{"`user`.is_admin": true},
			builder.NotIn("`user`.type", UserTypeIndividual, UserTypeBot),
		)))),
		builder.Exists(builder.Select("id").From("two_factor").Where(builder.Eq{"uid": userID})),
		builder.Exists(builder.Select("id").From("webauthn_credential").Where(builder.Eq{"user_id": userID})),
	)
}
```

```go
// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package organization

import (
	"context"

	auth_model "gitea.dev/models/auth"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
	"gitea.dev/modules/cache"
	"gitea.dev/modules/cachegroup"

	"xorm.io/builder"
)

type ignoreTwoFactorPolicyKey struct{}

// IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy returns a context in which no organization's two-factor policy blocks anyone.
// Code that writes or deletes rows based on a user's access (unassigning, unwatching, trimming allowlists)
// must use it, so a user who is only blocked until they enrol loses nothing.
func IgnoreTwoFactorPolicy(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
	return context.WithValue(ctx, ignoreTwoFactorPolicyKey{}, true)
}

// IsTwoFactorBlocked reports whether the organization requires two-factor authentication and u has
// neither TOTP nor WebAuthn, so u must be treated as a non-member: no member, team or collaborator access.
// Site admins and non-person identities (the organization itself pushing through a deploy key, Actions
// users, the ghost user) are never blocked. The enrolment check is cached per request.
func (org *Organization) IsTwoFactorBlocked(ctx context.Context, u *user_model.User) (bool, error) {
	if !org.RequireTwoFactor || u == nil || u.ID <= 0 || u.IsAdmin ||
		(u.Type != user_model.UserTypeIndividual && u.Type != user_model.UserTypeBot) {
		return false, nil
	}
	if ignore, _ := ctx.Value(ignoreTwoFactorPolicyKey{}).(bool); ignore {
		return false, nil
	}
	has, err := cache.GetWithContextCache(ctx, cachegroup.UserHasTwoFactor, u.ID, auth_model.HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	return !has, nil
}

// CountOrgMembersWithoutTwoFactor counts the organization's members enrolled in neither TOTP nor WebAuthn.
func CountOrgMembersWithoutTwoFactor(ctx context.Context, orgID int64) (int64, error) {
	return db.GetEngine(ctx).
		Where(builder.Eq{"`org_user`.org_id": orgID}).
		And(builder.Not{user_model.HasTwoFactorCond("`org_user`.uid")}).
		Count(new(OrgUser))
}

// CountOrgOutsideCollaboratorsWithoutTwoFactor counts the non-members who collaborate on any of the
// organization's repositories and are enrolled in neither TOTP nor WebAuthn.
func CountOrgOutsideCollaboratorsWithoutTwoFactor(ctx context.Context, orgID int64) (int64, error) {
	return db.GetEngine(ctx).Table("collaboration").
		Join("INNER", "repository", "`repository`.id = `collaboration`.repo_id").
		Where(builder.Eq{"`repository`.owner_id": orgID}).
		And(builder.NotIn("`collaboration`.user_id", builder.Select("uid").From("org_user").Where(builder.Eq{"org_id": orgID}))).
		And(builder.Not{user_model.HasTwoFactorCond("`collaboration`.user_id")}).
		Distinct("`collaboration`.user_id").
		Count()
}
```

```text
// IsUserRealRepoAdmin check if this user is real repo admin
func IsUserRealRepoAdmin(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, user *user_model.User) (bool, error) {
	if repo.OwnerID == user.ID {
		return true, nil
	}

	if err := repo.LoadOwner(ctx); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	accessMode, err := accessLevel(ctx, user, repo)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}

	return accessMode >= perm_model.AccessModeAdmin, nil
}

// IsUserRepoAdmin return true if user has admin right of a repo
func IsUserRepoAdmin(ctx context.Context, repo *repo_model.Repository, user *user_model.User) (bool, error) {
	if user == nil || repo == nil {
		return false, nil
	}
	if user.IsAdmin {
		return true, nil
	}

	mode, err := accessLevel(ctx, user, repo)
	if err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	if mode >= perm_model.AccessModeAdmin {
		return true, nil
	}

	for _, team := range teams {

		}
	}
	return false, nil
```

```text
// RecalculateReviewsOfficial re-evaluates the "official" flag of the latest approve
// and reject reviews of an issue against its pull request's current base branch.
// It must be called whenever the target branch changes, otherwise an approval that
// was official on the previous (possibly unprotected) branch would keep satisfying
// the new branch's protection rules.
func RecalculateReviewsOfficial(ctx context.Context, issue *Issue) error {
	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		return err
	}

	// Clearing and restoring the official flags must happen atomically, otherwise a
	// failure in between would leave the reviews without any official flag set.
	return db.WithTx(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
		// Only the latest approve/reject review of each reviewer counts as official, so
		// clear the flag on all of them first and restore it only where it still applies.
		if _, err := db.GetEngine(ctx).
			Where("issue_id = ?", issue.ID).
			In("type", ReviewTypeApprove, ReviewTypeReject).
			Cols("official").
			Update(&Review{Official: false}); err != nil {
			return err
		}

		reviews, err := FindLatestReviews(ctx, FindReviewOptions{
			Types:   []ReviewType{ReviewTypeApprove, ReviewTypeReject},
			IssueID: issue.ID,
		})
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		for _, review := range reviews {
			if err := review.LoadReviewer(ctx); err != nil {
				return err
			}
			if review.Reviewer == nil {
				continue
			}
			official, err := IsOfficialReviewer(ctx, issue, review.Reviewer)
```

```text
304	// userOrgTeamRepoBuilder returns repo ids where user's teams can access.
305	func userOrgTeamRepoBuilder(userID int64) *builder.Builder {
306		return builder.Select("`team_repo`.repo_id").
307			From("team_repo").
308			Join("INNER", "team_user", "`team_user`.team_id = `team_repo`.team_id").

312	// userOrgTeamUnitRepoBuilder returns repo ids where user's teams can access the special unit.
313	// A team grants the unit either through an explicit team_unit row (access_mode > none) or by being an
314	// admin/owner team (team.authorize >= admin), which grants every unit regardless of team_unit rows —
315	// mirroring the HasAdminAccess() short-circuit in access.GetIndividualUserRepoPermission.
316	func userOrgTeamUnitRepoBuilder(userID int64, unitType unit.Type) *builder.Builder {
317		return userOrgTeamRepoBuilder(userID).
318			Join("INNER", "team", "`team`.id = `team_repo`.team_id").
319			Join("LEFT", "team_unit", builder.Expr("`team_unit`.team_id = `team_repo`.team_id AND `team_unit`.`type` = ?", unitType)).
320			Where(builder.Or(
321				builder.Gte{"`team`.authorize": int(perm.AccessModeAdmin)},
322				builder.Gt{"`team_unit`.`access_mode`": int(perm.AccessModeNone)},
323			))
324	}
```

```text
func Members(ctx *context.Context) {
	org := ctx.Org.Organization
	ctx.Data["Title"] = org.FullName
	ctx.Data["PageIsOrgMembers"] = true

	page := max(ctx.FormInt("page"), 1)
	keyword := ctx.FormTrim("q")
	ctx.Data["Keyword"] = keyword

	opts := &organization.FindOrgMembersOpts{
		Doer:    ctx.Doer,
		OrgID:   org.ID,
		Keyword: keyword,
	}

	if ctx.Doer != nil {
		isMember, err := ctx.Org.Organization.IsOrgMember(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID)
		if err != nil {
			ctx.ServerError("IsOrgMember", err)
			return
		}
		opts.IsDoerMember = isMember
	}
	ctx.Data["PublicOnly"] = opts.PublicOnly()

	total, err := organization.CountOrgMembers(ctx, opts)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("CountOrgMembers", err)
		return
	}
```

```text
// DisableTwoFactor deletes the user's 2FA settings.
func DisableTwoFactor(ctx *context.Context) {
	if user_model.IsFeatureDisabledWithLoginType(ctx.Doer, setting.UserFeatureManageMFA) {
		ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusNotFound)
		return
	}

	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("settings_title")
	ctx.Data["PageIsSettingsSecurity"] = true

	t, err := auth.GetTwoFactorByUID(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID)
	if err != nil {
		if auth.IsErrTwoFactorNotEnrolled(err) {
			ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.Tr("settings.twofa_not_enrolled"))
			ctx.Redirect(setting.AppSubURL + "/user/settings/security")
		} else {
			ctx.ServerError("SettingsTwoFactor: Failed to GetTwoFactorByUID", err)
		}
		return
	}

	if err = auth.DeleteTwoFactorByID(ctx, t.ID, ctx.Doer.ID); err != nil {
		if auth.IsErrTwoFactorNotEnrolled(err) {
			// There is a potential DB race here - we must have been disabled by another request in the intervening period
			ctx.Flash.Success(ctx.Tr("settings.twofa_disabled"))
			ctx.Redirect(setting.AppSubURL + "/user/settings/security")
		} else {

func WebauthnDelete(ctx *context.Context) {
	if user_model.IsFeatureDisabledWithLoginType(ctx.Doer, setting.UserFeatureManageMFA) {
		ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusNotFound)

	}

	if _, err := auth.DeleteCredential(ctx, ctx.FormInt64("id"), ctx.Doer.ID); err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetWebAuthnCredentialByID", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.JSONRedirect(setting.AppSubURL + "/user/settings/security")
```

```text
// Copyright 2025 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package common

import (
	goctx "context"
	"errors"
	"sync"

	activities_model "gitea.dev/models/activities"
	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/log"
	"gitea.dev/services/context"
)

// StopwatchTmplInfo is a view on a stopwatch specifically for template rendering
type StopwatchTmplInfo struct {
	IssueLink  string
	RepoSlug   string
	IssueIndex int64
	Seconds    int64
}

func getActiveStopwatch(ctx *context.Context) *StopwatchTmplInfo {
	if ctx.Doer == nil {
		return nil
	}

	_, sw, issue, err := issues_model.HasUserStopwatch(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID)
	if err != nil {
		if !errors.Is(err, goctx.Canceled) {
			log.Error("Unable to HasUserStopwatch for user:%-v: %v", ctx.Doer, err)
		}
		return nil
	}

	if sw == nil || sw.ID == 0 {
		return nil
	}

	return &StopwatchTmplInfo{
		issue.Link(),
		issue.Repo.FullName(),
		issue.Index,
		sw.Seconds() + 1, // ensure time is never zero in ui
	}
}

func notificationUnreadCount(ctx *context.Context) int64 {
	if ctx.Doer == nil {
		return 0
	}
	count, err := db.Count[activities_model.Notification](ctx, activities_model.FindNotificationOptions{
		UserID: ctx.Doer.ID,
		Status: []activities_model.NotificationStatus{activities_model.NotificationStatusUnread},
	})
	if err != nil {
		if !errors.Is(err, goctx.Canceled) {
			log.Error("Unable to find notification for user:%-v: %v", ctx.Doer, err)
		}
		return 0
	}
	return count
}

type pageGlobalDataType struct {
	IsSigned    bool
	IsSiteAdmin bool

	GetNotificationUnreadCount func() int64
	GetActiveStopwatch         func() *StopwatchTmplInfo
}

func PageGlobalData(ctx *context.Context) {
	var data pageGlobalDataType
	data.IsSigned = ctx.Doer != nil
	data.IsSiteAdmin = ctx.Doer != nil && ctx.Doer.IsAdmin
	data.GetNotificationUnreadCount = sync.OnceValue(func() int64 { return notificationUnreadCount(ctx) })
	data.GetActiveStopwatch = sync.OnceValue(func() *StopwatchTmplInfo { return getActiveStopwatch(ctx) })
	ctx.Data["PageGlobalData"] = data
}
```

```text
// Collaboration render a repository's collaboration page
func Collaboration(ctx *context.Context) {
	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.settings.collaboration")
	ctx.Data["PageIsSettingsCollaboration"] = true

	users, _, err := repo_model.GetCollaborators(ctx, &repo_model.FindCollaborationOptions{RepoID: ctx.Repo.Repository.ID})
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetCollaborators", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["Collaborators"] = users

	teams, err := organization.GetRepoTeams(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository.OwnerID, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRepoTeams", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["Teams"] = teams
	ctx.Data["Repo"] = ctx.Repo.Repository
	ctx.Data["OrgID"] = ctx.Repo.Repository.OwnerID
	ctx.Data["OrgName"] = ctx.Repo.Repository.OwnerName
	ctx.Data["Org"] = ctx.Repo.Repository.Owner
	ctx.Data["Units"] = unit_model.Units

	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplCollaboration)
}
```

```text
package organization_test

import (
	"testing"

	"gitea.dev/models/organization"
	"gitea.dev/models/unittest"
	user_model "gitea.dev/models/user"
```
```go
	"gitea.dev/modules/structs"
```
